comment: One row per asset Blender makes (#801 to #808). `npm run blender:render <pack>` runs tools/blender/packs/<script> once per row, on one of Devon's machines with Blender 5.2, and writes assets/blender/<pack>/<name>.glb and its tools/blender/manifest.json row. Every key of a row is in its source hash, so editing a row without a render is check 8 line 4. `packs.<pack>.extraColours` is at most 8 colours outside tools/pixel/textures.json's palettes, each with a `why`.

extraColours.why: Tallow. The candle-count quest and the chapel candle clue are tallow candles, and the castle's palettes stop at plaster #cbbfa3, which reads as stone beside a wall of it, not as a candle.
Wheat, and the rick. The castle's palettes have no yellow above plaster #cbbfa3 and wooden_gate's browns, so a field of standing corn at 60 m in the fog would read as bare earth or as stone.

Meadow. Every green in tools/pixel/textures.json is forest_ground_06 or grassy_cobblestone, moss and shade at most #5b6a36, and a hay meadow beside a ploughed strip needs one green lighter than the slopes behind it, or the fields are one colour under fog.
Thatch, for the longhouse and barn roofs. The castle roofs are slate and tile, and a farm under a slate roof reads as a second castle at 100 m.

Skin. The castle's palettes are stone, wood, plaster and moss, and the nearest thing to a face in them is wood_floor_deck #a17f58, which reads as a wooden mask. `Bare`, so the tint never touches it (#820).
Skin, for the two old heads: paler and greyer than the first, so an old face differs from a young one by more than its brows at the distance a player passes one.

Undyed linen, the lightest `Cloth` swatch. The tint multiplies `Cloth`, so a garment can only be as light as its swatch, and the palettes stop at plaster #cbbfa3, which would darken every tint by a fifth (SPECS.md, "Two materials over the one atlas image"; #644, #684).

The pig's snout, and the geese's bills and feet. The castle's palettes have no pink: the nearest are castle_brick_02_red's #9a4430, which reads as a wound, and plaster #cbbfa3, which is the coat it has to stand out from. `Bare`, so a tint on the coat never touches it (#827).

Linen, the cloth on the high table. It is what tells the Constable's board from the household's trestles down the hall, and the castle's palettes stop at plaster #cbbfa3, which on a table reads as a second, paler wood. The same undyed linen the folk pack wears.

rows.name: crate
rows.why: The pipeline's proof end to end (#808): a store crate of planks and two battens, placed once in the larder.

rows.name: aumbry-candles
rows.why: Dresses the candle-count quest (four tallow in the aumbry at Compline, three at Lauds) and data/lore.json's candle account; the three that are left, at 26, 22 and 18 cm. Not pressable, so no clue (#810).

rows.name: pricket
rows.why: Swaps for the `candle` evidence, `candles-chapel` (#811): one tallow candle in a pricket at the first turn of the Chapel Tower stair, wax pooled below it. The photoscanned brass candleholders it replaces were three candlesticks in a 1.08 m spread and 41,936 triangles.

rows.name: knife-barrel
rows.why: Swaps for the `knife` evidence (#811), a herring: the kitchen knife, in the bakehouse, flour on it. A flour barrel with the knife stuck in the flour and its handle over the rim, in place of a kit barrel.

rows.name: ledger-desk
rows.why: Swaps for the `ledger` evidence, `table-muniment` (#811): the works ledger open on a desk in the muniment room, 340 sheets received and 212 laid, in place of a photoscanned table with nothing on it.

rows.name: backdrop-north
rows.why: North of the base ground, the whole north walk's view: fields under the wall, two farmsteads, woods on the slopes and the rim at z -170. One of five pieces cut from one height field (#817); placed as interiorProps `backdrop-north`, backdrop and noCollide.

rows.name: backdrop-south
rows.why: South of the base ground: fields, two farmsteads and the rim at z 170. One of five pieces cut from one height field (#817); placed as interiorProps `backdrop-south`, backdrop and noCollide.

rows.name: backdrop-east
rows.why: East of the base ground, between the north and south pieces: fields running out to the rim at x 180. One of five pieces cut from one height field (#817); placed as interiorProps `backdrop-east`, backdrop and noCollide.

rows.name: backdrop-north-west
rows.why: North of outside-ground, beside the town: woods and the rim along the river's line at x -140, so the north end of the river runs under a hill and not into nothing. One of five pieces cut from one height field (#817); placed as interiorProps `backdrop-north-west`, backdrop and noCollide.

rows.name: backdrop-south-west
rows.why: South of outside-ground: one farmstead and the rim, as the north-west piece. One of five pieces cut from one height field (#817); placed as interiorProps `backdrop-south-west`, backdrop and noCollide.

rows.name: folk
rows.why: The household's shared body (#820 to #823): one 20-joint rig, 22 parts in five slots a person picks from by `parts`, and eleven clips. `rig` is each joint's place in metres in the model frame (+x the body's left, +y up, +z the way it faces); every joint keeps the model's own axes, so a joint's rotation at rest is none. `parts` is the catalogue, one mesh node each, `Cloth` tinted and `Bare` not. `clips` is tools/bodies/clips.json's grammar over this rig's own Idle: the angle at key k of `keys` is rest + amp * sin(2 pi (cycles * k / keys + phase)), a rotation about a model axis at the joint, composed on Idle's at that key; `cycles` is an integer or the clip does not loop, and `driver` is the joint test/assets.mjs holds 20 degrees off Idle. `sheet` is the six people the contact sheet lines up. The first wearer is the hen-wife.

rows.name: mallet
rows.why: The carter's mallet, for his `hammer` stop at the cart (#800): a rigid file on `heldProp`, because a skinned tool would be one more skinned draw per holder (#820). A beech head on an ash haft with two iron bands, stood on its haft so +Y runs from the grip to the head.

rows.name: pig
rows.why: The hen-wife's pig, in the outer ward by her patch (#829): the low barrel, the snout and the short legs are what read as a pig at 10 m, and the snout's disc is the one face the tint must not touch.

rows.name: goat
rows.why: The inner ward's goat (#829): narrow, leggy, horned and bearded, so it is not a small sheep. The horns are why #827's length to height is 1.15 and not the cow's 1.3.

rows.name: sheep
rows.why: One sheep beside the cow (#829): the fleece is `Coat`, so a tint makes a white or a dark sheep off one file as the two hens are one file (#684); the face and legs are `Bare` and stay dark.

rows.name: horse
rows.why: The horse by the porter's lodge (#829), the only animal taller than a child: long legs, a raised neck, and a mane and tail in `Bare` so a bay stays black-pointed under any tint.

rows.name: cat
rows.why: The bakehouse cat (#829), a mouser at 0.3 m: pointed ears, a long tail carried behind it and green eyes, which is everything a cat is at the distance a player sees one.

rows.name: goose
rows.why: The hen-wife's geese (#829), two off one file by tint: a long neck stood straight up, a heavy body carried level on two legs set under it, and a pink bill and feet in `Bare`. The bird topology, 12 joints (#826), because a quadruped's front legs are wings on nothing.

rows.name: kitchen-worktable
rows.why: The kitchen's working board (#814): a board on trestles with a dough trough and two pots on it, so the room the cook stands in reads as where the castle's bread and pottage are made. Devon's hearth crane, spit and oven are the fire (#830); this is the table between them.

rows.name: kitchen-shelves
rows.why: A standing rack of crocks against the kitchen wall (#814): three shelves, eight crocks, the stores a kitchen keeps to hand. It stands on the floor and collides; a shelf hung clear of a head would be at 1.9 m, where nobody could reach a crock.

rows.name: hall-trestle
rows.why: The household's table in the great hall (#814): a trestle board and a bench down each side, placed twice. data/lore.json seats the household in the hall at Vespers, and the hall had one photographed table for all of them.

rows.name: hall-high-table
rows.why: The high table on the dais, where data/lore.json seats the Constable and his lady (#814): a longer board under a linen cloth and one bench behind it, so whoever sits there faces down the hall.
